headline: The F20 is a DUAL-IDENTITY receiver. With no controller associated it enumerates as a vendor HID device (413d:2106, Zikway 'HID zk', usage page 0xFF7A, 64-byte unfragmented reports, no kernel input node). The moment the ArmorX/Xbox assembly associates wirelessly it DISCONNECTS on the same physical port 1-7 and re-enumerates as a Microsoft Xbox controller (045e:0b12, bcdDevice 5.18) with the xpad driver and a real /dev/input/js0.

vendor_mode.endpoints: 0x83 IN interrupt 64 B bInterval 8; 0x03 OUT interrupt 64 B bInterval 8
vendor_mode.receiver_alone_traffic: 12 interrupt IN URBs and 3 interrupt OUT URBs over 155 s, NONE carrying data; last activity t=73.6 s, then silence. No periodic reports at all.

xbox_mode.interface0: xpad bound, 2 endpoints: 0x02 OUT 64 B bInterval 4, 0x82 IN 64 B bInterval 2
xbox_mode.nodes: /dev/input/js0 and event18, handlers kbd event18 js0; /proc/bus/input/devices Name=Microsoft Xbox Series S|X Controller
xbox_mode.traffic: 17,164 interrupt IN URBs vs 3 before association; 26 control transfers; GIP traffic at roughly 8 ms cadence
